reconstructed_theorem: For every real number β>0 and every natural number N (including N=0), define μ=β/[2(N+1)] and f:ℝ→ℝ by f(x)=μx²/2. Then μ>0; f is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable; f is globally μ-strongly convex, meaning that for every x,y∈ℝ and t∈[0,1], f((1−t)x+ty)≤(1−t)f(x)+tf(y)−(μ/2)t(1−t)|y−x|²; for every x,y∈ℝ it satisfies f(y)≤f(x)+f′(x)(y−x)+(β/2)|y−x|²; and 0 is a global minimizer, i.e. f(0)≤f(x) for every x∈ℝ. In addition, let T:ℝ→ℝ be T(x)=x−(1/β)f′(x), and let z=T iterated N times starting at 1 (equivalently x₀=1, xₖ₊₁=xₖ−(1/β)f′(xₖ), z=x_N). Then f(z)−f(0)=β/[4(N+1)]·(1−1/[2(N+1)])^(2N), and β/[16(N+1)]≤f(z)−f(0). Here μ and f depend on both β and the chosen horizon N; the same fixed f is used throughout those N iterations. At N=0 iteration is the identity and z=1; the displayed exponent 2N is zero and its power equals 1. The gradient in the formal statement is the actual Fréchet-gradient, identified here with f′ for this smooth real scalar function. The modulus μ is asserted to be a valid strong convexity lower bound, with no assertion that it is maximal.
objects: β∈ℝ, N∈ℕ, μ=β/(2(N+1)), f:ℝ→ℝ given by μx²/2, T(x)=x−β⁻¹f′(x), z=T^[N](1).
quantifiers: Universal β subject to β>0; universal N≥0. The strong convexity and upper quadratic bound quantify over all real x,y; the chord parameter is any t∈[0,1].
assumptions: Only β>0; N is any natural number. Smoothness, strong convexity, the upper quadratic bound and minimization are conclusions about the explicitly defined f.
scopes: μ and f are defined after β and N are chosen and scope all subsequent conclusions; z is defined for the final equality and lower bound. Initial iterate is exactly 1, minimizer exactly 0, and iteration count exactly N.
constant_dependencies: Strong convexity modulus μ=β/(2(N+1)); upper quadratic coefficient β/2; fixed gradient step 1/β; exact gap prefactor β/(4(N+1)); geometric factor (1−1/(2(N+1)))^(2N); lower gap β/(16(N+1)).
